## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?

6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.

## 1. Those who brought the lie  (`#those-who-brought-the-lie`)

Cited ayat: 24:11-15

> **24:11** إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِٱلْإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِّنكُمْ لَا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَّكُم بَلْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ لِكُلِّ ٱمْرِئٍ مِّنْهُم مَّا ٱكْتَسَبَ مِنَ ٱلْإِثْمِ وَٱلَّذِى تَوَلَّىٰ كِبْرَهُۥ مِنْهُمْ لَهُۥ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
>
> **24:12** لَّوْلَآ إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتُ بِأَنفُسِهِمْ خَيْرًا وَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَآ إِفْكٌ مُّبِينٌ
>
> **24:13** لَّوْلَا جَآءُو عَلَيْهِ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فَإِذْ لَمْ يَأْتُوا۟ بِٱلشُّهَدَآءِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلْكَٰذِبُونَ
>
> **24:14** وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ لَمَسَّكُمْ فِى مَآ أَفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
>
> **24:15** إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُۥ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِكُم مَّا لَيْسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ وَتَحْسَبُونَهُۥ هَيِّنًا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (24:11): Those who brought the ifk, a grave falsehood, were a group among those addressed.

**c2** (24:11): They are told not to think it bad for them; rather it is good for them.

**c3** (24:11): Each of them will have what he earned of sin, and the one who took the greater part of it upon himself has a great punishment.

**c4** (24:12): The verse asks why, when they heard it, the believing men and women did not think well of themselves and say that this is a clear lie.

**c5** (24:13): The verse asks why they did not bring four witnesses for it; since they did not bring the witnesses, those, in God's sight, are the liars.

**c6** (24:14): Were it not for the favour of God upon them and His mercy, in this world and the hereafter, a great punishment would have touched them for what they plunged into.

**c7** (24:15): They received it with their tongues and said with their mouths what they had no knowledge of, and counted it light, while with God it is grave.

### One-minute summary

The verses say that a group among those addressed brought a grave falsehood, the ifk [c1]. They say that the believing men and women should have thought well and said that it is a clear lie [c4], and that, since the witnesses were not brought, those are the liars in God's sight [c5]. They say that without God's favour and mercy a great punishment would have touched them [c6].

### Complete story

Those who brought the ifk, a grave falsehood, were a group among those addressed [c1]. They are told not to think it bad for them; rather it is good for them [c2]. Each of them will have what he earned of sin, and the one who took the greater part of it upon himself has a great punishment [c3].

The verse asks why, when they heard it, the believing men and women did not think well of themselves and say that this is a clear lie [c4]. It asks why they did not bring four witnesses for it; since they did not bring the witnesses, those, in God's sight, are the liars [c5].

Were it not for the favour of God upon them and His mercy, in this world and the hereafter, a great punishment would have touched them for what they plunged into [c6]. They received it with their tongues and said with their mouths what they had no knowledge of, and counted it light, while with God it is grave [c7].

### Deep study

The verses name no person and give no content of the falsehood; they speak of a group, of each one's share, and of the one who took the greater part [c1][c3]. The passage turns from those who brought it to those who heard it, and asks what the hearers should have done [c4][c5]. It states in its own words that those who did not bring the witnesses are the liars in God's sight [c5]. It also speaks of passing on, with the tongue and the mouth, what one has no knowledge of, and of counting light what is grave with God [c7].

### Kids mode

The verses say that a group brought a grave falsehood [c1]. They say that when the believers heard it they should have thought well and said that it is a clear lie [c4]. They say that what one has no knowledge of is grave with God, even if people count it light [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage turns attention from those who spread a falsehood to what those who hear it should do [c4]. Another is that it names saying what one has no knowledge of as grave with God [c7].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what the falsehood said, whom it concerned, who the group was, who took the greater part of it, or when and where it happened. The verses name no one, and this draft names no one.
- Not established: what 'think well of themselves' covers; the Arabic says 'of their own selves', and the verse does not say more.
- The verse about the witnesses (24:13) is stated here as it is written, and the draft draws no further conclusion from it.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: an occasion for these verses, the person the falsehood concerned and the persons given as having spread it. None is used, and this draft names no one.

## 2. What should have been said  (`#what-should-have-been-said`)

Cited ayat: 24:16-20

> **24:16** وَلَوْلَآ إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُم مَّا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّتَكَلَّمَ بِهَٰذَا سُبْحَٰنَكَ هَٰذَا بُهْتَٰنٌ عَظِيمٌ
>
> **24:17** يَعِظُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَن تَعُودُوا۟ لِمِثْلِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
>
> **24:18** وَيُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلْـَٔايَٰتِ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
>
> **24:19** إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَ أَن تَشِيعَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةُ فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
>
> **24:20** وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (24:16): The verse asks why, when they heard it, they did not say that it is not for them to speak of this, glory be to God, this is a great slander.

**c2** (24:17): God admonishes them never to return to the like of it, if they are believers.

**c3** (24:18): God makes the signs clear to them, and God is knowing and wise.

**c4** (24:19): Those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe have a painful punishment in this world and the hereafter; God knows and they do not know.

**c5** (24:20): The verse repeats 'were it not for the favour of God upon you and His mercy', and says that God is kind and merciful.

### One-minute summary

The verses ask why the hearers did not say that it is not for them to speak of this, and that it is a great slander [c1]. God admonishes them never to return to the like of it, if they are believers [c2]. They end with God's favour and mercy [c5].

### Complete story

The verse asks why, when they heard it, they did not say that it is not for them to speak of this, glory be to God, this is a great slander [c1].

God admonishes them never to return to the like of it, if they are believers [c2]. God makes the signs clear to them, and God is knowing and wise [c3].

Those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe have a painful punishment in this world and the hereafter; God knows and they do not know [c4]. The passage ends by repeating that it is by the favour of God upon them and His mercy, and that God is kind and merciful [c5].

### Deep study

The passage gives words that the hearers might have said, and calls the falsehood a great slander [c1]. It then admonishes and turns to a wider warning about those who love that indecency should spread [c2][c4]. The verse about those who love that it spread speaks of them and not of those who brought the falsehood [c4]. The passage closes with favour and mercy, as it did in the earlier verses [c5].

### Kids mode

The verses ask why the hearers did not say that it is not for them to speak of this [c1]. God admonishes them never to return to the like of it, if they are believers [c2]. God makes the signs clear, and God is knowing and wise [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage gives the hearers words to say as well as a warning [c1][c2]. Another is that it ends, as it began, by pointing to God's favour and mercy [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what 'indecency' refers to here, or how it relates to the falsehood of the previous chapter; the verse speaks of those who love that it spread.
- Not established: who 'they' are who are admonished, beyond those addressed in the passage.
- Not established: which 'signs' God makes clear.
- Not established: how the punishment in this world and the hereafter is carried out; the verse says only that it is painful.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the occasion and the persons concerned. None is used, and this draft names no one.
